news.title: Afterpay Reaches $2.68 Million California Underwriting Settlement
news.body: PYMNTS reports that California’s Department of Financial Protection and Innovation reached a $2.68 million settlement with Afterpay over underwriting failures. The amount describes the settlement total, not an established penalty-only figure. The underwriting action concerns Afterpay’s lending practices and is separate from the Block AML matter referenced in the report.

news.title: Highnote Applies to Establish a National Bank
news.body: Highnote filed applications with the OCC and FDIC to establish a national bank, Banking Dive reports. The applications seek regulatory approval; they do not establish an approved charter or launch date. The report establishes no immediate change to existing customer programs or sponsor-bank relationships.

news.title: Capital One Details Payments Modernization and Fraud-Model Work
news.body: In an interview with Banking Dive, a Capital One executive described the bank’s payment-rail architecture and remaining modernization work, including ACH and wire migration. The executive also outlined fraud-model work aimed at reducing false positives and increasing approvals. Those are stated objectives: the interview supplied no measured improvements.

news.title: South Korea Proposes Rules for Bank-Issued Won Stablecoins
news.body: South Korea has proposed rules allowing local banks to issue won-pegged stablecoins, according to Finextra. The proposal would create a bank-issuance route rather than establish that banks have already launched tokens. Issuer eligibility, redemption obligations and distribution permissions will define how banks can offer the proposed instruments.

news.title: Aave Labs Publicly Launches Savings App With Reported Balances Above $63 Million
news.body: Aave Labs has publicly launched its savings app, with balances exceeding $63 million, The Block reports. The launch expands public access, but the reported balance does not measure net inflows or withdrawal performance. Customers assessing the app need to distinguish its yield sources and protection arrangements from those of an insured bank deposit.

perspective: Highnote seeks banking authorization while Capital One outlines payment-rail modernization, spanning charter applications and infrastructure investment.

curiosity.text: In 1946, Flatbush National Bank of Brooklyn introduced its “Charge-It” plan: customers charged purchases at participating local merchants, who submitted the sales slips to the bank for payment. Unlike a modern card network, the arrangement served the bank’s own customers and nearby merchants. Source: Smithsonian National Museum of American History — https://americanhistory.si.edu/collections/object-groups/credit-cards
